title: Phase Contrast 4D-STEM Tomography of Thick Biological Specimens
content: Four-dimensional scanning transmission electron microscopy (4D-STEM) is routinely used to characterize materials at high resolution, across large fields of view. Recently, phase retrieval techniques such as multi-slice ptychography [1] have enabled super-resolution and show promise for imaging radiation-sensitive materials with high sensitivity. This phase sensitivity is particularly relevant for biological specimens, where contrast emerges primarily from phase shifts as electrons traverse light atoms in vitreous ice. While early work demonstrated 4D-STEM's potential in single particle analysis at moderate resolutions [2], and more recent work has achieved resolutions up to 5.8 Å [3], its broader application to biological imaging remains in early stages.
